intro.text: The young emperor of Azir, the Prime Aqasix, who is cautious about Dalinar Kholin's attempts to unite Roshar.
The young emperor of Azir, a former street thief named Gawx who was made Prime after Lift saved his life.
The young emperor of Azir and a member of Dalinar Kholin's coalition, once a street thief named Gawx.

items.text: As a boy named Gawx, Yanagawn broke into the palace in Azimir with his uncle Huqin and Lift to steal. They were caught, and he was mortally wounded by one of a stranger's attendants. Lift healed him, and the viziers, seeing a miracle, proclaimed him Prime Aqasix on the spot. His first act was to pardon Lift and save her from execution.

As emperor, Yanagawn was expected to study and to be on display; people even watched him eat and sleep, for in Azir the emperor belongs to the people. When Lift went to Yeddaw he asked the scribes of the Grand Indicium to treat her as they would him, and he kept in touch, asking her to come back.

When Dalinar asked to meet through the Oathgate to discuss uniting Roshar, Yanagawn and his advisors refused, implying the gate was broken. They thanked him for the warning about the Everstorm and reported that the awakened parshmen in Azir were negotiating contracts rather than attacking.

Dalinar brought Yanagawn into the vision of Aharietiam. Terrified at first, the emperor then wandered off to question the people there and recognised Jezerezeh'Elin when the Herald declared victory. He told Dalinar he saw him as an enemy and an Alethi who still revered the Sunmaker, and he and Lift left together.

After more visions, the vision of the Recreance shook Yanagawn. He admitted to Dalinar that he did not feel ready to rule, and that he held back because Lift distrusted Dalinar for seeming too righteous.

Lift changed her mind about Dalinar after seeing him face Odium, and persuaded Yanagawn to receive him in Azimir. Dalinar gave the Prime and his viziers three essays, which impressed them, Navani's most of all, and they accepted his invitation to Urithiru.

Yanagawn was the first to arrive at Urithiru, with an ornate throne and representatives from Emul, Yezier and Tashikk. He backed their claims to territory, questioned Dalinar's new power and the Radiants of old, but once his people were tasked with a code for sharing resources, Azir joined and offered five battalions.

When the coalition fractured after Taravangian's treachery, the Azish withdrew from Urithiru. On the way home Yanagawn wanted to turn back to help the Alethi, trusting Lift's faith in Dalinar, but news that Amaram's army had changed sides left him thinking they had been wrong to trust them.
With Dalinar, Jasnah, Taravangian and Fen, Yanagawn approved the expedition to the honorspren city of Lasting Integrity and the military campaign in Emul.
Grown more confident, he began to ignore Azish traditions, taking off his headdress and letting Jasnah and Dalinar sit at his own height when they met at his warcamp.

Adolin taught Yanagawn military strategy through the game of towers and showed him how to use Shardplate, encouraging him to take a more active role than his advisors wanted. They became close friends, and Yanagawn refused to abandon Adolin during the Battle of Azimir.
Yanagawn became one of the Unoathed, bonding a formerly deadeye spren named Xorm, and gained a Shardblade and Shardplate that can regrow.

appearance.text: Yanagawn is a lanky, dark-skinned youth whose limbs seem too long and whose face is round and childlike. He was fifteen when the Everstorm first came.

personality.text: When he first became Prime, Yanagawn was unsure of himself and knew he wasn't really ruling. Over time he grew confident, no longer embarrassed among viziers and scions and no longer startled at being called 'Your Majesty'.
Yanagawn trusts Lift's judgement, and his view of Dalinar changed as hers did. He learned from her that it is wrong to betray a friend.
His power is absolute in theory but held in check by the Azish government. He speaks Alethi, though not fluently, and practises his speeches before meeting the other monarchs.
